item.title: 49ers pivoted to Keenan Allen trade after initially focusing on Josh Downs
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The 49ers made a trade for wide receiver Keenan Allen on Tuesday, but he wasn't the only Colts wide receiver on their radar ahead of the trade deadline.
item.content:encoded:
The 49ers made a trade for wide receiver Keenan Allen on Tuesday, but he wasn't the only Colts wide receiver on their radar ahead of the trade deadline.

During a Thursday appearance on KNBR, General Manager John Lynch said that the team turned its attention to Allen after initially targeting Josh Downs as an addition to their receiver room. Lynch said that head coach Kyle Shanahan brought up Allen while watching film on Downs and conversations with the Colts began before they landed defensive tackle DeForest Buckner in an earlier deal with Indianapolis.

"We kind of focused on Josh Downs as an option that we'd have some interest," Lynch said, via 49ersWebzone.com. "And Kyle and I are kind of watching Josh, and in the process, Kyle's like, 'Man, what about Keenan?' And I was like, 'You know, we hadn't given much thought to that, but let me ask about that.' And so, there started a conversation about two and a half weeks ago, really, when the DeForest talks [happened]. 'Would he?' And it's always fluid, and at a certain time, they didn't want to give up Keenan. It kind of wasn't going to be on the table, but we kept communicating, and ultimately we got him."

The 49ers sent a 2027 sixth-round pick to the Colts for Allen. Downs and a 2027 seventh-round pick were eventually traded to the Chiefs for 2027 fourth- and fifth-round picks.

item.title: Bengals designate Andrei Iosivas, two others for return from IR
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Bengals will have three players back at practice on Thursday.
item.content:encoded:
The Bengals will have three players back at practice on Thursday.

They announced that they have designated wide receiver Andrei Iosivas, cornerback Jalen Davis, and guard Brian Parker for return from injured reserve. All three players will be able to practice with the team for the next 21 days and they can return to the active roster at any point in that window.

Iosivas has been out since Week 2 with a thumb injury. He had three catches for 19 yards in the first two weeks of the season and had 69 catches over the previous two seasons.

Davis played in the first three games and has been out with a hamstring injury. He had five tackles, a tackle for loss and a pass defensed before his injury.

Parker was a sixth-round pick this year and landed on injured reserve ahead of Week 1.

item.title: Lions vs. Patriots matches up this year's two most aggressive head coaches on fourth downs
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: When the Lions meet the Patriots in Munich on Sunday, the fans in Germany are likely to see both teams go for it on fourth down.
item.content:encoded:
When the Lions meet the Patriots in Munich on Sunday, the fans in Germany are likely to see both teams go for it on fourth down.

That's because Lions head coach Dan Campbell has long been the league's most aggressive coach on fourth downs, and this year, Patriots coach Mike Vrabel is No. 2.

Coaches' fourth down decisions are tracked for the Aggressiveness Index at FTN Fantasy, looking at how often coaches go for it compared to other coaches in the same situation. By that measurement, Campbell is first with a score of 1.45 (meaning he goes for it 45 percent more than an average NFL coach) and Vrabel is second with a score of 1.22.

The Aggressiveness Index is a more detailed way of tracking a coach's fourth-down decision making than simply looking at the number of times a team has gone for it on fourth down. Some teams go for it often on fourth down not because the coach is aggressive, but because they happen to face a lot of fourth-and-shorts while trailing late in the fourth quarter. That's not a particularly aggressive time to go for it.

What gives Campbell such a high score on the Aggressiveness Index is decisions like going for it on fourth down at his own 24-yard line with the score tied late in the fourth quarter against the Packers. That's the kind of call that Campbell makes and other coaches don't, which is why his Aggressiveness Index is so much higher than any other coach's.

Campbell is at or near the top of the Aggressiveness Index every year. Last year he was second only to Mike Kafka, who was very aggressive on fourth downs during his seven-game stint as the Giants' interim head coach. Perhaps unsurprisingly, after Kafka was not retained by the Giants, Campbell hired him to be the Lions' passing game coordinator.

Vrabel has not been as aggressive as Campbell on fourth downs, but he has been more aggressive than the average NFL coach, both during his time with the Patriots and before that as head coach of the Titans. Both Vrabel and Campbell are former players with reputations for a blend of old-school toughness and a new-school understanding of the strategic advantages of aggressive fourth-down decision making. It's a winning combination.

item.title: PFT's Week 10 2026 NFL picks
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: I have no explanation for the last two weeks.
item.content:encoded:
I have no explanation for the last two weeks. But I'll use an unexpected run of success to provide a warning to anyone else who wakes up one day in the midst of a hot streak.

In Week 8, I went 13-1 in the straight-up-only picks exercise. (No more picks against the spread, for reasons I've previously explained.) For Week 9, I ended up 14-1.

That's 27-2 over two weeks. (Which translates to 87-48-1 for the year, which doesn't sound nearly as good as "27-2.")

Now for the warning, specifically to anyone who has gambled or who will be gambling on sports. The worst thing you can do is get lucky. Because you'll think that you've suddenly become good.

Then, you'll let it ride until your luck runs out. That's when it gets dangerous. Because you'll fool yourself into thinking that it's just a temporary setback, that your secret formula for picking winners remains viable, and you'll chase your losses. You'll keep digging that hole, confident that it's just a matter of time before your sudden genius returns.

Eventually, you'll find yourself in an untenable financial situation.

That's how it happens for plenty of gamblers. They don't start out losing and keep losing. They win enough to make themselves think they know more than they do, when the reality is that no one knows anything. And then the wheels come off. And then they get desperate to put the wheels back on.

Case in point: Last week, someone who has been part of the NFL universe for more than 30 years expressed amazement that the Cowboys were favored by only 4.5 points against the Colts. With the Colts in disarray due to multiple trades and poised to make even more trades, the Cowboys would win easily. It was, the person said, a "sure thing."

Final score? Cowboys 27, Colts 23.

There is no sure thing in gambling. Well, there's one. If you ever let yourself believe you're smarter than the house and you don't snap out of it in time, it's a sure thing that you'll be filing for bankruptcy, eventually.

Commanders at Giants (Thursday night)

Can Dan Quinn and company come up with another way to screw things up in a key moment?

Giants 23, Commanders 17.

Patriots vs. Lions (Germany)

It's desperation time for New England, like it was when they found a way to beat the Bills.

Patriots 23, Lions 20.

Chiefs at Falcons

The Falcons are capable of winning every game. It's just impossible to know when that version of the team is going to make an appearance.

Chiefs 27, Falcons 17.

Texans at Browns

Time is running out on Houston. And the Browns seem to be in the early stages of a backslide.

Texans 20, Browns 16.

Vikings at Packers

One of the craziest weeks in Vikings history ends on a high note, thanks to the Packers not being able to run the ball effectively.

Vikings 24, Packers 20.

Dolphins at Colts

With the uncertainty of the trade deadline over, the Colts can get back to focusing on trying to win football games.

Colts 17, Dolphins 7.

Panthers at Saints

If the Saints can put a full 60 minutes together, they could be very dangerous.

Saints 27, Panthers 20.

Bills at Jets

The Bills have a rough six-game stretch coming; they know not to fall victim to a trap game.

Bills 30, Jets 17.

Jaguars at Titans

Liam Coen and Robert Saleh meet again. One has an elite roster. One does not.

Jaguars 24, Titans 13.

Rams at Cardinals

The Cardinals still can't figure out how to win a game at home.

Rams 17, Cardinals 13.

Seahawks at Raiders

It'll take a little time to get Fernando Mendoza fully up to speed.

Seahawks 16, Raiders 9.

49ers at Cowboys

If it wasn't already clear that the Cowboys are a long way from being elite, it will be.

49ers, 31, Cowboys 20.

Steelers at Bengals

Joe Burrow's MVP case gets even stronger with a prime-time win.

Bengals 27, Steelers 23.

Chargers at Ravens

Jacoby Brissett's job is simple. Win a few winnable games so that the team will still be relevant when Lamar Jackson returns.

Ravens 14, Chargers 6.

item.title: Trevor Lawrence: Trades show the confidence in our team, what we have a chance to do
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: The Jaguars signaled they're all-in on the 2026 season by making several trades to fortify their roster before the deadline.
item.content:encoded:
The Jaguars signaled they're all-in on the 2026 season by making several trades to fortify their roster before the deadline.

Quarterback Trevor Lawrence told reporters in his Wednesday press conference that the moves signal a positive trend for the team.

"I think you try not to look too much into it,” Lawrence said, via transcript from the team. “We have the same job to do, and I think we have a really good team that has good chemistry. Has gelled together. We like playing together, we have great camaraderie. All those things that are just hard to put your finger on sometimes. I think we have all that. I think we've been playing well, and so we still have a job to do, and nothing changes from that perspective.

“But I do think, obviously with the moves made, I think it shows the confidence in our team, and what we have the chance to do. I think that we're a really good team, and now we get even better with these guys. I think that's all it is, is just making our team even better, and we know that we're going to have a shot. We just got to keep playing well and we got to keep winning. I think you can't look too much into it because we still have the same job right in front of us, but I think these guys are going to help us for sure.”

Moreover, it helps that the players acquired have significant postseason experience.

“I think to get winners, to get guys that have been there before, that experience is important,” Lawrence said. “I think that is, why would you not want that if you can? Obviously, you got to look at the players you're getting, and you want great players, but if they've also won Super Bowls and been to Super Bowls, I think that's icing on the cake or whatever. That's a plus. So, we have some guys obviously in that group that have done that. Just excited to get that experience. I think they've played meaningful football. They know what it looks like and going to add that value to our team.”

We’ll see how the additions start to fit in when the Jaguars play the Titans on Sunday.

item.title: PFT's Week 10 2026 NFL power rankings
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The Bills benefit from facing another backup QB.
item.content:encoded:
1. Bills (last week No. 1; 7-1): If they'd been playing a team with a borderline functional offense, they may have surrendered the top spot to Jacksonville.

2. Jaguars (No. 2; 6-2): Who cares about future draft picks when the AI apocalypse is coming?

3. 49ers (No. 3; 7-1): It feels like they'll be up to something on trade-deadline day.

4. Broncos (No. 4; 7-2): They're good enough to win the games they try to lose.

5. Bears (No. 5; 7-2): Caleb Williams isn't trying to become Patrick Mahomes; he's hoping to morph into Michael Jordan.

6. Chiefs (No. 7; 6-2): The kicker position shouldn't be a pick-your-poison proposition.

7. Steelers (No. 8; 6-2): Completing the sweep of the Bengals will be critical to winning the division.

8. Bengals (No. 11; 6-2): A Super Bowl push is very realistic.

9. Seahawks (No. 9; 5-4): Drew Lock fits this team better than Sam Darnold does.

10. Lions (No. 12; 6-2): What's German for kneecap?

11. Packers (No. 14; 6-3): When Micah Parsons returns, they could make a major move.

12. Vikings (No. 6; 6-2): Tuesday is arguably the most pivotal non-game day for the Vikings in years; will they upgrade at quarterback?

13. Giants (No. 16; 5-2-1): They're gradually pulling away in the NFC East.

14. Patriots (No. 10; 5-4): The regression continues.

15. Rams (No. 15; 5-4): Can Ty Simpson play receiver?

16. Browns (No. 13; 5-4): Can they stop the bleeding?

17. Raiders (No. 17; 4-5): It's time to flip the Fernando switch.

18. Buccaneers (No. 18; 3-6): They'd be dangerous on the road in the playoffs, if they can get there.

19. Ravens (No. 19; 4-5): Can they hold it together until Lamar Jackson returns?

20. Texans (No. 23; 3-5): C.J. Stroud is earning millions by the week.

21. Saints (No. 25; 3-5): Suddenly, they're tied for first place in the division.

22. Panthers (No. 22; 3-5): David Tepper is going to pull out all the stops in an effort to land Mike Tomlin.

23. Cardinals (No. 20; 3-6): Good news, Carson Beck — you're playing. Bad news, Carson Beck — you're playing.

24. Falcons (No. 21; 3-6): The Jessie Bates trade says it all; they're not interested in winning the division and getting blown out by the No. 5 seed in the wild-card round.

25. Cowboys (No. 26; 4-5): Even the games against the bad teams are a struggle.

26. Commanders (No. 24; 2-5-1): The mini-bye could be the time to bid farewell to the head coach.

27. Eagles (No. 27; 2-7): The soft-shell tank is on.

28. Titans (No. 28; 1-7): No one would have even noticed they were on a bye, but for whatever it was that happened with Calvin Ridley.

29. Colts (No. 29; 2-7): Vaya con dios, Jonathan Taylor.

30. Dolphins (No. 30; 1-7): The only drama left is whether they finish last in the division.

31. Jets (No. 31; 2-7): Same.

32. Chargers (No. 32; 0-8): Do they know they're winless?

item.title: Longtime Steelers player, coach Dick Hoak dies at 86
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Steelers announced the death of their longtime player and coach Dick Hoak at the age of 86.
item.content:encoded:
The Steelers announced the death of their longtime player and coach Dick Hoak at the age of 86.

Hoak was born outside of Pittsburgh and went to Penn State before the Steelers made him a 1961 seventh-round pick. He spent 10 years as one of the team's running backs and finished his career with 3,965 rushing yards and 1,452 receiving yards. Hoak scored 33 overall touchdowns during his time on the roster.

Hoak joined Chuck Noll's staff as an offensive backfield coach in 1972, moved to running backs coach in 1991 and was the only one of Noll's coaches who remained on the staff under Noll's successor Bill Cowher. He retired in 2006 after coaching future Hall of Famers Franco Harris and Jerome Bettis and being part of five Super Bowl champions.

"We are deeply saddened by the passing of Dick Hoak, a legendary member of the Pittsburgh Steelers family," Steelers owner Art Rooney II said in a statement. "Dick was part of the foundation of this organization and played an instrumental role in shaping the Steelers as both a player and coach during his 45 years with the team. Dick represented everything the Steelers stand for with his toughness, loyalty, dedication and an unwavering commitment to the team. First as a player, then as a coach, Dick's contributions to this organization spanned generations."

Hoak is a member of the Steelers' Hall of Honor and received the Pro Football Hall of Fame's Award of Excellence in 2025.

item.title: Report: Ravens to sign K Harrison Mevis to practice squad
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Ravens had a pair of kickers in for workouts on Wednesday and they'll reportedly keep them both around for a while.
item.content:encoded:
The Ravens had a pair of kickers in for workouts on Wednesday and they'll reportedly keep them both around for a while.

There was word on Wednesday that they will be signing former Dolphins kicker Riley Patterson and NFL Media reports on Thursday that they will also sign Harrison Mevis to their practice squad.

Mevis played in the first five Rams games of the season, but he was released after missing a pair of field goals in their overtime loss to the Bills last month. He was 5-of-9 on field goals this season and 12-of-13 in nine games for the Rams last season.

The Ravens put Tyler Loop on injured reserve ahead of Week 9 and elevated Jake Moody from the practice squad for their last game. Moody signed with the Falcons this week and the Ravens will now have a choice to make about who handles their kicking duties against the Chargers on Monday night.

item.title: For Week 9, Next Gen Stats outpaced the McAfee alt cast again
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The ESPN announcement of the viewership for a given Monday night game always requires a careful look for any information about the viewership of the multiple weekly alt casts on the Disney-owned networks.
item.content:encoded:
The ESPN announcement of the viewership for a given Monday night game always requires a careful look for any information about the viewership of the multiple weekly alt casts on the Disney-owned networks.

This week, the release presented only the total viewership for all platforms, at 21.7 million. The release also mentioned that multppe alt casts "averaged more than 900K viewers."

Andrew Marchand of The Athletic has gotten the numbers. For the Next Gen Stats alt cast, 499,000 tuned in. For the McAfee ensemble, the number was 406,000. Making the total audience 905,000.

The final tally gives Next Gen Stats a 2-0 lead over the McAfee option. The gap was more narrow this time around; when they first squared off for the Week 6 Commanders-49ers game, NFLN attracted 469,000 and ESPN2 got 351,000. (ESPN2 is in roughly 70 million homes; NFL Network's distribution is at or below 50 million.)

The total viewership for that game was 17.9 million. With Bills-Vikings beating that figure by 21.2 percent, Next Gen Stats was up 6.3 percent over Week 6 and the McAfee cast increased by 15.6 percent.

Of the total audience for the game, 2.2 percent watched NFL Network and 1.87 percent watched ESPN2. Which raises, once again, a one-word question: Why?

The Monday night alt casts don't draw in new viewers. It's added expense, with no extra revenue for the broader operation. (Unless there's a tangible benefit to siphoning viewers from ABC/ESPN for the other channels.)

Ultimately, it's a zero-sum game. With alt casts, Bills-Vikings viewership was 21.7 million. Without alt casts, Bills-Vikings viewership undoubtedly would have been 21.7 million.

And that's why the various ABC affiliates are upset that Disney will have a full slate of alt casts for Super Bowl LXI. The total number will be the total number, if the game is on one network or twenty. The alt casts will rob the Peter of ABC to pay the Paul of the various other platforms.

item.title: Carson Beck "super excited" to make his debut on Sunday
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Cardinals rookie quarterback Carson Beck will make his first start on Sunday against the Rams.
item.content:encoded:
Cardinals rookie quarterback Carson Beck will make his first start on Sunday against the Rams.

Speaking to reporters in a Wednesday press conference, Beck said he’s “super excited” to make his regular-season debut.

“Obviously, having gone from the emergency quarterback at the beginning of the season to last week being the backup to now being the starter, it’s been a crazy season,” Beck said, via transcript from the team. “It’s really been a welcome to the NFL season, just getting introduced to what the league is and what it can be, but I'm super excited for the opportunity and to have the chance to go play with these guys.”

Beck will be the third starting quarterback for the Cardinals this season after Jacoby Brissett and Gardner Minshew. Beck noted he’s picked up plenty from observing both veteran QBs to this point in the year.

“I think the biggest thing is just watching those two and how they carry themselves and how they handle themselves not only in the meeting room around the coaches, but during the walkthrough, during practice, and during the game,” Beck said. “I think that’s the biggest thing that you can learn from those guys, of everybody’s looking at you as a quarterback, and your attitude has to be right each and every day. The moxie [of] going out there, having confidence, and making everyone around you better.

“I think that’s something that I learned in how they carry themselves and when they went on the field — how I need to carry myself as well.”

To that end, Beck said “of course” he can maintain his sense of confidence entering Sunday.

“I think the coolest thing about confidence is that confidence is a choice,” Beck said. "With that also, I’ve said it before, it makes everyone else around you better as well. It exudes confidence into them when you’re showing that you’re confident. When you can choose that, again, you just have to go out there and execute. You have to go out there and do your thing and you have to go out there and be confident, have swag, and have moxie. Regardless of the circumstances, regardless of anything going on around you, regardless of maybe what happened the play before or maybe thinking about what’s going to happen the next play.

“You have to be in the present moment and that’s really all you can do and control.”

item.title: Source: Daiyan Henley failed Broncos physical
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Knee issue caused Denver to scrap trade with Chargers.
item.content:encoded:
When word emerged that the trade that would have sent linebacker Daiyan Henley from the Chargers to the Broncos was called off, no specific details were provided. Common sense pointed to a failed physical and, for a change, common sense was accurate.

Per a source with knowledge of the situation, Henley did indeed fail the physical in Denver.

It was, we're told, a knee issue. Although Henley appeared on the Week 9 injury report with a shoulder problem, he was listed with a knee injury in Week 6.

Every trade hinges on the passing of a physical. The player rarely fails it. Still, when he does, the trade doesn't happen.

The problem with eleventh-hour deadline deals that fall through is that the team that thought it was acquiring a new player now can't pivot elsewhere.

Of course, there's always the possibility that the Broncos got cold feet after committing a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick to the transaction. As everyone learned with the failed Maxx Crosby trade from the Raiders to the Ravens, the standards can shift from team to team.

Crosby, who stayed with the Raiders, has started all nine games — and he has been on the field for 89 percent of the snaps. Henley, who has started all eight Chargers games and played 87 percent of the snaps, presumably will return to action for the Chargers.

item.title: Fernando Mendoza: Starting is a "new step," but it's not a whirlwind
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Everyone knew that it was only a matter of time before Fernando Mendoza became the Raiders' starting quarterback, but the first overall pick in this year's draft said on Wednesday that he was taken by surprise when he learned the time had come.
item.content:encoded:
Everyone knew that it was only a matter of time before Fernando Mendoza became the Raiders' starting quarterback, but the first overall pick in this year's draft said on Wednesday that he was taken by surprise when he learned the time had come.

While many people speculated that Kirk Cousins would be traded to the Vikings ahead of Tuesday's deadline, Mendoza said he had "no inkling" that a trade was coming before he learned Cousins was headed back to one of his former teams. Mendoza thanked Cousins for his mentorship on and off the field several times during a press conference and said that relationship has built his belief that he can succeed at the helm of the offense in Las Vegas.

Mendoza described moving into the starting lineup as "a new step," but not one that he views as a whirlwind because of the work that he's put in since joining the team.

"I'm a lot more confident as a quarterback and feel more developed, whether it's under center, connecting with teammates, understanding an NFL scheme," Mendoza said. "There are so many areas that I have improved on, and I look forward to keep on improving because there’s still a lot of work to do."

That next chapter of work will begin against the Seahawks this weekend and facing the defending champs won't be an easy way to kick off life as a starter, but it will be a good way of learning just what Mendoza will be up against as he tries to grow as an NFL quarterback.

item.title: Report: Giants called Falcons about a potential Bijan Robinson trade
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: The Giants didn't make any big deals at the trade deadline, but they tried to make a very big one.
item.content:encoded:
The Giants didn't make any big deals at the trade deadline, but they tried to make a very big one.

The Giants called the Falcons to see whether running back Bijan Robinson was available in a trade, according to Jordan Raanan of ESPN.

That would have been a blockbuster, but it's unsurprising that the teams didn't make a deal. The Falcons made a big investment in Robinson this offseason, signing him to a three-year, $66.8 million contract extension, and from all accounts they view him as one of the most important pieces of their franchise.

There's no word on what the Giants were willing to offer, or whether the Falcons engaged at all, or simply told the Giants, "Not interested."

The Giants did make one big trade this season, acquiring J.J. McCarthy, who has played well enough for the Giants to win their first two starts and remain in first place in the NFC East. Acquiring Robinson would have been a strong sign that the Giants believe they're serious contenders, this year. That the Giants even tried showed that coach John Harbaugh meant it when he said they're a team trying to win now, not build for the future.

item.title: Todd Monken: I intend for Deshaun Watson being our starting QB
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Monken said he doesn't anticipate making a quarterback change while confirming Watson's Week 10 return.
item.content:encoded:
Browns head coach Todd Monken opened his Wednesday press conference by confirming that Deshaun Watson will be back as the team's starting quarterback for their Week 10 game against the Texans.

Watson did not play last week after missing a pair of practices while in the concussion protocol and the team's plans for this Sunday remained a topic of conversation because Monken declined to say who would start during a Monday press conference. Monken explained that response by saying that he wanted to talk to the team's coaching staff before adding that he also didn't feel a need to make a public proclamation.

"Ultimately, the full body of work, the previous eight games we had played," Monken said. "Deshaun played pretty well. That was my intention, I just wanted to make sure to run it by my staff before I said it publicly. I don't know why I have to say it publicly."

Monken was asked if he will be making a quarterback determination on a weekly basis moving forward.

“I don’t look at it week-to-week and I don’t look at it as long term," Monken said. "We're judged each week. I am, he is, our team is. . . . I anticipate him being our starter. That's what he's been, he’s been our starter. . . . I have no intention of Deshaun not being our starter."

The Texans are 5-4 heading into their game with the Texans and they have a bye in Week 11. If they are unable to stay on the right side of .500 after that break, Monken will likely field more questions about the plan for Watson moving forward.

item.title: Broncos, Chargers announce Daiyan Henley will not be traded after all
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: More than 24 hours after the NFL trade deadline, the trade of Henley from the Charges to the Broncos was canceled.
item.content:encoded:
Just before Tuesday afternoon's trade deadline, the Chargers agreed to trade linebacker Daiyan Henley to the Broncos. Late on Wednesday night, the trade was canceled.

Both the Chargers and the Broncos have announced that Henley will remain with the Chargers. Neither team explained why, but typically that would happen after the trade deadline only if the player failed his physical.

"The proposed trade involving Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley will not be finalized," the Broncos said in a statement. "We have great respect for Daiyan as a player and person, and we wish him all the best moving forward."

The Chargers posted "Welcome back, Daiyan" on social media, about 30 hours after posting, "Thank you, Daiyan" to officially announce the trade.

According to ESPN, Henley was at the Broncos' facility on Wednesday and took a physical, so presumably the Broncos' medical staff decided to nix the trade. Henley did suffer a shoulder injury in Week 8 against the Rams, but he was a full participant in practice the next week and played well in Week 9 against the Texans. There have been no indications that he has had any other health concerns.

The Broncos had agreed to send a 2027 fourth-round draft pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick to the Chargers for Henley, who is in the final year of his rookie contract and is slated to become an unrestricted free agent in March.

item.title: Kevin O'Connell on Kyler Murray: I want him to get healthy, you never know what could happen
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Vikings made Kyler Murray their quarterback choice to open the 2026 season, but it didn't take long for their plans to go awry.
item.content:encoded:
The Vikings made Kyler Murray their quarterback choice to open the 2026 season, but it didn't take long for their plans to go awry.

Murray was concussed early in the season opener, missed Week 2 and then led an underwhelming offense to a 4-1 record before suffering a hamstring injury in Week 8. The Vikings offense got even worse with Carson Wentz in Monday night's loss to the Bills, which led the team to trade for Kirk Cousins on Tuesday.

Head coach Kevin O'Connell hasn’t committed to starting Cousins against the Packers this weekend, but it's why the deal was made and Murray isn't currently an option because he remained out of practice with a hamstring injury on Wednesday. Once Murray is healthy, he'll be slated for a backup role as O'Connell said he doesn't believe "you can have a competition during the season" and that his hope is that Murray is available if and when the Vikings have to pivot again.

“The reality is what it is," O'Connell said. "It’s one of those things where I think he appreciated hearing about it before the transaction took place, but at the same time, he knows I believe in him. I believe in Kyler, just like I believe in Carson and I believe in Max [Brosmer]. I want him to get healthy and get back to work because you just never know. We do not hold the cards in how this will go from a health standpoint or anything like that with anybody on our team.”

O'Connell said that he told Murray that he knows it has been a "less than ideal" series of events, but that underscores the possibility that the Vikings will have to turn back to him with an important game on the line at some point later this year.

item.title: Vikings are in the four-quarterback club, for now
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The Vikings' addition of quarterback Kirk Cousins comes with a surprising decision on the back end.
item.content:encoded:
The Vikings' addition of quarterback Kirk Cousins comes with a surprising decision on the back end.

Minnesota has not released any of its other quarterbacks. Giving the Vikings four quarterbacks on their 53-man roster.

With Cousins on the team, Kyler Murray, Carson Wentz, and Max Brosmer remain. It's amazing, frankly, that Wentz hasn't been cut; Monday night's performance shows that he should no longer be playing in the NFL. Or the UFL. Or the CFL. Or any organization that ends with "FL."

It's hard to imagine Wentz sticking around for long. The Vikings possibly have decided to keep Wentz for now, given that Murray still has a hamstring injury.

Regardless, the soft benching of Murray has now become a hard benching. And the hard benching of Wentz inevitably will become a pink slip.

They're all in with Cousins. The longer he plays, the better chance the Vikings have to make it to the playoffs.

It starts on Sunday, despite coach Kevin O'Connell being coy about it. Cousins undoubtedly will play. That's why he's there.

Even if he's not 100-percent ready, a less-than-prepared Cousins is better than the other options they have.

item.title: Kirk Cousins plans to talk to Jakobe Thomas about No. 8
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Vikings quarterback Kirk Cousins made his official return to the team on Wednesday.
item.content:encoded:
Vikings quarterback Kirk Cousins made his official return to the team on Wednesday. He still doesn't officially have a number.

Has he spoken to rookie safety Jakobe Thomas, who currently wears No. 8?

"I need to circle back with him," Cousins told reporters. "Haven't gotten there. So we'll have a conversation and I think Mike Parsons will help us, too, in the equipment room. But, yeah, I've got to talk to Jakobe for sure."

When the issue came up again later, Cousins laughed — while also making his intentions clear: "I'm confident that Jakobe and I can have a healthy and mature conversation and figure this out."

It's hard to imagine Thomas standing in Cousins's way. There are too many Vikings fans who still have No. 8 jerseys that will become moot if Cousins isn't wearing it.

However it goes, it would be a shock if Cousins isn't wearing No. 8 on Sunday at Lambeau Field.

item.title: Daniel Jones is "not happy" with Colts' roster purge
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The Colts had a mini-fire sale in recent weeks, trading away four starters for future assets.
item.content:encoded:
The Colts had a mini-fire sale in recent weeks, trading away four starters for future assets.

Quarterback Daniel Jones, not surprisingly, isn't thrilled by the decision to send guard Quenton Nelson, defensive tackle DeForest Buckner, receiver Keenan Allen, and receiver Josh Downs to other teams.

"I mean, honestly, you’re not you’re not happy to see it, right?" Jones said. "You're a player and you're going out there competing and doing everything you can to win games. So you're not happy to see a lot of those decisions, and — but like I said, it's outside of our control, and our job is to play, be prepared, and play well.  So, like I said, we got a lot of trust in the guys coming in to those spots, and we'll be ready to go."

It's a bad situation for the players who remain, since it will be harder for them to win with backups thrust into the lineup. But that's how it works whenever a non-contender admits its situation and trades players.

Those who remain have to keep going, trying to win games even if they get the impression that the front office doesn't really care.

And even though the Jets hold the Colts' first-round pick, a bad season for Indianapolis will result in a higher spot in every round. As the Colts embark on a rebuild, it's not crazy to think the front office hopes to sink as low in the standings as possible, since that will enhance the priority of the picks they have.

The Jets will welcome that, since they have the Colts' first-round pick. Thanks to the failed trade for cornerback Sauce Gardner.

item.title: Bengals call off trade for Arnold Ebiketie
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Tuesday morning brought word that the Bengals had agreed to acquire pass rusher Arnold Ebiketie in a trade with the Eagles, but that agreement will not be finalized ahead of the 4 p.m.
item.content:encoded:
Tuesday morning brought word that the Bengals had agreed to acquire pass rusher Arnold Ebiketie in a trade with the Eagles, but that agreement will not be finalized ahead of the 4 p.m. ET trade deadline.

According to multiple reports, the Bengals have called off the trade and will not be sending a 2027 sixth-round pick to Philadelphia.

The reports surfaced shortly after a tweet by OverTheCap.com contributor Nick Korte explained the compensatory pick ramifications of the deal. According to Korte, who focuses on the compensatory pick system, acquiring Ebiketie would put the Bengals in position to forfeit the third-round compensatory pick that they are currently set to receive for Trey Hendrickson leaving the team to sign with the Ravens.

That would greatly increase the price that the Bengals were going to pay to acquire Ebiketie and it appears they found it too high to move forward with the deal.

item.title: Zac Taylor: Duke Tobin is "really apologetic" after backing out of trade with Eagles
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: On Tuesday, the Bengals backed out of a trade for edge rusher Arnold Ebiketie after it was revealed that the deal might cost Cincinnati with a future compensatory draft pick.
item.content:encoded:
On Tuesday, the Bengals backed out of a trade for edge rusher Arnold Ebiketie after it was revealed that the deal might cost Cincinnati with a future compensatory draft pick.

During his Wednesday press conference, head coach Zac Taylor explained the situation from the perspective of Bengals director of player personnel — and de facto General Manager — Duke Tobin.

"Obviously, we tried something yesterday," Taylor said. "Duke was very explicit with me when he came and spoke to me about how he wanted this portrayed. I'm not comfortable doing it, but I'm going to do what he asked. We did make an effort to put some depth in there in place of Cashius [Howell]. As we got into it, it was going to be more costly than we initially anticipated.

"He's really apologetic about it and wants it made clear — Philly was a great trade partner. It was on our end. Certainly, we have a ton of confidence in our front office and how they do things. They've given us the players that have allowed us to be 6-2 right now, and playing at such a high level. So, we’ll put that behind us and move forward, and just get excited for this game on Sunday. Our locker room is in a great place right now."

Taylor noted Tobin didn’t really tell him how everything went down and he didn’t ask the question.

“It doesn’t really matter to me. It probably took three minutes of my day yesterday away from watching tape,” Taylor said. “So, got a lot of faith in how those guys operate and we’ll just move forward with it.”

With that, the Bengals didn’t make any deadline moves to improve the team. Taylor said he and Tobin like where the team is.

“I think you can talk to the players in the locker room, they really like where we’re at,” Taylor said. “So, this is a team with a lot of confidence right now. I know it’s a fun period of time — the weeks leading up to the trade deadline — for fans … but the truth is, we really like where we’re at. Our guys are playing with a high degree of confidence and we’ll continue to move forward.”

item.title: Ravens not planning change to starting offensive line after Ryan Neuzil trade
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Ravens made a trade for center Ryan Neuzil this week, but they aren't planning on throwing him right into the lineup in Week 10.
item.content:encoded:
The Ravens made a trade for center Ryan Neuzil this week, but they aren't planning on throwing him right into the lineup in Week 10.

Neuzil started every game for the Falcons this season and he also made 17 starts in 2025. The Falcons' offensive line coach in 2025 was current Ravens offensive line coach Dwayne Ledford, so Neuzil feels he understands "what [Ledford] wants and what he sees in the linemen."

That knowledge should help Neuzil pick things up on the fly, but head coach Jesse Minter said Neuzil's arrival doesn't mean current center Cam Jurgens will be knocked out of the lineup.

"I think he brings versatility," Minter said, via the team's website. "I don't anticipate anything changing with Cam and what position he plays. We think he's like the future of our offensive line. I think it's just a piece that adds depth. I do think he'll have flexibility as he gets here, as he gets going. Wherever that leads I think we'll see as we go."

The Ravens have had to change plans at center multiple times since Tyler Linderbaum's departure during the offseason. If they need to make another one, Neuzil will give them an experienced option to plug the hole.

item.title: Dolphins QB Kyle McCord: Experience in big games something I can draw from
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Dolphins placed Malik Willis on injured reserve this week and that means Kyle McCord will be making his first NFL start when they face the Colts on Sunday.
item.content:encoded:
The Dolphins placed Malik Willis on injured reserve this week and that means Kyle McCord will be making his first NFL start when they face the Colts on Sunday.

It will also be McCord's first regular season action and first game snaps of any kind with the Dolphins. The 2025 sixth-round pick spent last season on the Eagles' practice squad and spent the summer with the Packers before being traded to Miami at the end of August.

That's a lot of firsts for one game, but McCord said his time at Ohio State and Syracuse is "something that you definitely can hang your hat on" because it gave him experience on big stages.

"It's a blessing, but I think once you get the first play call on the helmet and get going, I think it'll feel just like football," McCord said, via a transcript from the team. "And I feel like going back to what I was just saying, that's something that having played in those big college games, I think you've been in those moments before. It's not my first time I'm playing in a big game. So yeah, I feel like that's where I'm drawing a lot of confidence from."

McCord would not be doing himself any favors by making more of the moment than it is, but that first play call and first snap against NFL opposition will likely lead to a quick realization that it's a different world from his last time in the saddle for a meaningful game.

item.title: Sean McVay laughs as he says he's tempted to ask assistant coach Robert Woods to suit up
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: He didn't sound completely serious, but Rams coach Sean McVay said on Wednesday that he talked to assistant wide receivers coach Robert Woods about whether he could suit up and play while receivers Puka Nacua, Davante Adams and Jordan Whittington are all out with injuries.
item.content:encoded:
He didn't sound completely serious, but Rams coach Sean McVay said on Wednesday that he talked to assistant wide receivers coach Robert Woods about whether he could suit up and play while receivers Puka Nacua, Davante Adams and Jordan Whittington are all out with injuries.

McVay was asked during his press conference whether he has talked to the 34-year-old Woods, who was a receiver for the Rams for five years, about potentially playing again.

“I have, yes," McVay answered with a laugh.

McVay acknowledged that there are Collective Bargaining Agreement rules against a coach becoming a player, but he said Woods is still in great shape and it would be fun to give it a try.

"I've looked at him, and the way he looks out there, I've definitely been tempted," McVay said. "I think that’d be a violation of the CBA. I don’t know what he’d have to do, but he looks damn good and still is smooth out there. Very tempting."

Woods was cut by the Steelers before the 2025 season and hasn't played since, and he announced his retirement and signed a one-day contract with the Rams in February of 2026. Realistically, even with his intimate knowledge of the Rams' offense, he probably wouldn't be able to contribute as much on the field as whatever receiver the Rams could add off waivers or another team's practice squad.

If Woods and the Rams actually wanted him to become an active player, it wouldn't be as simple as signing him to the active roster, as the league has rules preventing that. Players on the reserve-retired list have to pass through waivers before they can join a team. And the NFL generally doesn't allow coaches to become players: In 2020, when the Broncos lost all their quarterbacks to covid, they asked the league office if they could activate one of their assistant coaches and were told no. In 2009, Eagles coach Andy Reid wanted to play coaching intern Matt Nagy at quarterback in a preseason game and was also told by the league that he couldn't.

So the idea of Woods playing receiver for the Rams is probably not going to get any kind of serious consideration. Even if, with all the Rams' injuries, it's tempting.

item.title: Sean McVay optimistic that Trent McDuffie will play Sunday vs. Cardinals
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Rams cornerback Trent McDuffie has missed three games this season and was listed as a non-participant in Wednesday's practice with a back injury, but the outlook for his ability to play Sunday against the Cardinals is good.
item.content:encoded:
Rams cornerback Trent McDuffie has missed three games this season and was listed as a non-participant in Wednesday's practice with a back injury, but the outlook for his ability to play Sunday against the Cardinals is good.

Coach Sean McVay said on Wednesday that McDuffie wants to go and the only question for the Rams is whether he'll be able to do everything he needs to do in a game, which can't always be simulated on the practice field.

"He's feeling good. We're optimistic this week he will be able to go," McVay said. "He's so damn tough, but you want to make sure that you're putting him in a position to have a successful outcome, and he is making really good progress. It's really just being able to deal with the functional movements and some of the unpredictability."

Injuries have taken a major toll on the Rams this season, and McDuffie is one of the big-name players in Los Angeles who hasn't made the impact the team was hoping to see, in large part because he hasn't been fully healthy. But when asked about McDuffie on Wednesday, McVay answered, "Hopefully this is the week."

item.title: Packers-Patriots on Fox leads Week 9 with 25.7 million
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: As NFL games go, the 4:25 p.m.
item.content:encoded:
As NFL games go, the 4:25 p.m. ET window routinely has the biggest audience of the week — larger than any prime-time game.

That was true on Sunday, when 25.7 million on average tuned in for the window headlined by the Packers shredding the Patriots, 45-27.

It was the most-watched telecast of the week on any network, besting the Bills-Vikings game on Monday night by 4.0 million.

As the NFL is looks for more windows, and potentially heads toward more Wednesday night (and possibly Tuesday night) games, 4:25 p.m. ET on Sunday continues to be the best slot.

Currently, that window is shared by CBS and Fox, with one or the other having the game in most weeks. (A few times per year, they both have 4:25 p.m. ET games on the same day.) With all windows (except for Monday night, which is available a year later) opening up in 2030, it will be interesting to see whether the NFL decides to stop splitting all of Sunday afternoon between two networks and selling 4:25 p.m. ET as a weekly package.

Given the audiences generated by that window, it would easily generate the biggest rights fee of any of them.

item.title: Keenan Allen says his beef with Mike Evans is in the past
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Keenan Allen says his beef with Mike Evans is in the past.
item.content:encoded:
Keenan Allen says his beef with Mike Evans is in the past.

Allen joined Evans in the 49ers' wide receivers room this week after a trade from the Colts.

"We squashed it a long time ago," Allen said Wednesday, via David Bonilla of 49erswebzone.com. "Everybody wants to bring it back up, obviously. But no, Mike's a hell of a player. He’s probably better than me at this point."

In a memorable 2020 back-and-forth on social media, Allen and Evans engaged in a spirited debate about who was the better wide receiver.

Allen was ranked 77th on the NFL Top 100 that season. Tyreek Hill ranked 22nd, Evans 30th and Chris Godwin 38th. Allen argued that he was better than Hill, Evans and Godwin.

"Ok I’m tired of biten my tongue...@cheetah @MikeEvans13_ @chrisgoodwin... ( and the list goes on) ARE NOT a better receiver than me! Faster than me...every day of the week but separation..CHILD PLEASE!" Allen wrote in his post.

Evans responded, "You tagged the wrong Chris Godwin lol and don’t be mad at us we ain’t make the rankings or care about em. I like the confidence but be realistic you not on my level bro."

Allen, who is in his 14th season, has 1,095 catches for 12,402 yards and 71 touchdowns and is a six-time Pro Bowler. Evans, who is in his 13th season, has 893 catches for 13,472 yards and 111 touchdowns and is a six-time Pro Bowler.

item.title: Dianna Russini's return includes no specifics about multiple controversies
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: As expected, Dianna Russini made her return to sports media on Wednesday, with a one-hour show platformed by an illegal offshore sports book.
item.content:encoded:
As expected, Dianna Russini made her return to sports media on Wednesday, with a one-hour show platformed by an illegal offshore sports book.

It's hardly a prime gig, but her "crisis publicist" managed to create plenty of hype — and to finagle a puff piece with People.com that included no questions about the circumstances that prompted Russini's resignation from The Athletic.

In September, the New York Post reported that Russini would "share her side of the scandal upon taking her next job." She hasn't, and she didn't in the debut episode of her new show.

Technical difficulties delayed the release of the first episode, which was supposed to be live but seemed to be entirely pre-recorded. (The company blamed the glitch on a "record-breaking audience." Comparable to what?)

Once the episode finally appeared, it featured three guests (none of whom are current players or coaches), preceded by a segment in which she addressed the future of Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson. Which, from an editorial standpoint, is hardly the top story in the NFL on the day after the trade deadline.

There was nothing new or particularly insightful about Jackson. It was a summary of the facts that anyone who has been paying attention to the situation already knew, with a not-groundbreaking assertion that the Ravens want to keep him beyond 2026.

More significantly, the wooly mammoth in the mud room was not addressed. The overriding message was that she went away for a while, she went through some things, and now she's back. For anyone who doesn't know the story, she said nothing that would even begin to shed light on it.

If it's going to be an opinions-and-interviews show, that's fine. If she's going to include the reporting of facts about the NFL, the credibility question can't be ignored.

And this isn't about the relationship (or whatever it was) with Patriots coach Mike Vrabel. It's about how she responded to it.

She issued a strident denial when the Post published the photos of the two of them at a resort in Arizona. One week later, she abruptly resigned from her position at The Athletic, complaining that "commentators in various media have engaged in self-feeding speculation that is simply unmoored from the facts."

In the months since making that assertion, she hasn't shared her own version of the facts. In her kid-gloves interview with People.com, Russini said that the “lies became so out of control.” Without identifying even one of the alleged lies.

Her nothing-to-see-here position was undermined by Vrabel himself, who abandoned his initial position that the initial photos "show a completely innocent interaction and any suggestion otherwise is laughable." Then came another group of photos, from March 2020, which had a distinct know-it-when-you-see-it vibe as to the specific nature of the relationship. That prompted Vrabel to step away from the team for the all-important third day of the draft, in order to attend counseling with his family.

So, to date, Russini's official position is that it was all a big nothing. Vrabel’s words and actions make it clear that it was something, whatever it was. (That boat-trip video didn't help much, either.)

Beyond the fact that The Athletic concluded, following an internal investigation, that "Russini’s relationship with Vrabel was in clear violation of The Athletic’s standards," the situation creates clear questions of credibility. Put simply, and bluntly, can the audience believe what she says?

That leads to the other issue, which has been largely overlooked in connection with her return to sports media — if a one-hour show hosted by an illegal offshore sports book even counts as that. In February, she told the story of being pulled over for texting while driving. She claimed that she FaceTimed a current head coach to get her out of the ticket. And, based on the bodycam footage released by the local authorities, that contention was flat-out false.

Forget the relationship with Vrabel. All insiders have compromised their journalistic integrity, in one way or another. The interests of the audience often take a back seat to the broader chess match of getting and staying in position to get "scoops" (which usually come in the form of a five-minute heads-up before a transaction is announced). Punches are pulled. Relevant stories are overlooked or downplayed. Favors are done for sources.

It's one thing to be compromised. It's another thing to have real issues when it comes to telling the truth. Because the fundamental premise of anyone who is engaged in reporting of any kind is that they are at all times telling the truth.

Even in post-truth America, it's a standard that should never be relaxed.

Russini's credibility has been damaged by her denials regarding the relationship (whatever it was) with Vrabel, and by Vrabel's actions that undercut her denials. Moreover, the casual, nonchalant spinning of a phony yarn about FaceTiming a coach to get out of a ticket makes it even harder to believe anything she says.

That's why I said last Saturday on #PFTPM that we'll be ignoring any of her reports until her credibility is somehow restored, if that's even possible at this point. In this business, it would be very easy to make assertions and couch them as news from an unnamed source. When someone has not one but two concrete instances of clear issues when it comes to telling the truth, it would be irresponsible for us to blindly accept any reports from that reporter and to use them here.

It's that simple. People may not like some of the things we report, but the goal at all times is to be fully and completely honest with the audience. Part of that duty of honesty includes being brutally honest that the word of someone who has, in multiple ways, damaged her own credibility simply can't be trusted here.

item.title: NC State moves even closer to hiring Philip Rivers
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Rivers, who played for the Wolfpack from 1999 through 2003, is now poised to coach them.
item.content:encoded:
Don't expect Philip Rivers to come out of retirement again this season. He'll be busy.

Via ESPN, the NC State board of trustees is expected to finalize a contract that will make Rivers the next head coach of the Wolfpack.

Rivers played for NC State from 1999 through 2003. He was the fourth overall pick in the 2004 draft, technically of the Giants. He was traded to the Chargers (with Eli Manning going to New York), and Rivers played for the Chargers through 2019. He spent 2020 with the Colts, and he unexpectedly returned late in the 2025 season to play for the Colts again.

Rivers became a high-school coach in Alabama in 2021. He has never coached at the college or pro level, but he interviewed for the Bills' head-coaching job.

It's not known whether he still aspires to coach at the NFL level. As he gets experience at NC State — and if he does well — buzz could build for a shot with an NFL team.

For now, he'll be returning to the place where he played college football. His name surfaced almost immediately after long-time coach Dave Doeren was fired last month. Along the way, NC State interviewed fellow former NC State quarterback (and NFL quarterback and current CBS analyst) Russell Wilson.

item.title: Kamario Taylor lands $7.5 million deal to return to Mississippi State
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: One man's chaos is another man's ca-ching.
item.content:encoded:
One man's chaos is another man's ca-ching.

After years of being stuck in a system that prevented them from getting fair (or any) value for their skills, efforts, and/or sacrifices, college football players are finally getting paid. And one of them is setting a new bar.

Via On3.com, Mississippi State quarterback Kamario Taylor is finalizing a $7.5 million deal to return in 2027. With incentives, it could yield as much as $9 million.

With Taylor under center, the Bulldogs started 4-0. Taylor has since suffered a season-ending injury.

Before the injury, Taylor was regarded as one of the favorites to win the Heisman Trophy.

While the development will prompt the pearl-clutchers to try to parlay the situation into more political momentum for the Protect College Sports Act, it's a reflection of the free market at work. Which is fine for those in positions of wealth and power, when it comes to their own financial position.

When someone else is reaping the benefits of capitalism in a way that complicates the lives of those who have to balance the books (and to pry cash from boosters who support the NIL funds), it becomes a problem.

And so they'll do whatever they have to do to roll back the gains players have made. Because free enterprise is desirable only when the people in control practice it.

When the workers start getting paid according to their worth, it becomes a crisis.
